record.title: PreDE reports a policy-specific gate for screening robot-policy quantization before closed-loop tests
record.summary: Xu et al. introduce PreDE, which calibrates policy-specific thresholds from a small set of quantized configurations with known closed-loop outcomes, then uses action deviation on a fixed observation log to accept, reject or defer new candidates. In the paper, 21 of 28 held-out configurations across Cosmos Policy and UVA received decisions, all matching their observed labels; seven were deferred, including both acceptable and degraded outcomes. A separate 450-trial Franka Research 3 study reports significant degradation for configurations assigned to high-deviation groups before trials, while low-deviation results were not statistically significant. W4A4 reduced median action-query latency 1.37× and peak memory about 44% on the tested setup. These are author-reported results, conditional on each policy and evaluation setting.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that PreDE issued decisions for 21 of 28 held-out configurations across two policies (75% coverage), and all issued decisions matched the observed acceptable or degraded labels; seven candidates were deferred.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a separate 450-trial Franka Research 3 study, the authors report significant degradation for every tested high-deviation configuration selected before trials; low-deviation comparisons did not reach significance, which does not establish equivalence.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the reported RTX 5080 setup, W4A4 reduced median action-query latency by 1.37× and peak allocated memory by about 44% relative to bf16.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: PreDE’s thresholds are policy- and setting-specific, and its accept/reject interpretation is conditional on a within-setting ordering hypothesis; uncertain cases require closed-loop evidence.

evidence_gaps.description: PreDE prediction results and repository code have not been independently executed or reproduced.
The real-robot low-deviation comparisons are too small to establish non-inferiority; PreDE’s threshold results are limited to two simulation-calibrated policies.

brief.importance_rationale: If validated across more policies and tasks, policy-specific offline screening could reduce the number of expensive robot or simulator rollouts needed to compare quantization configurations, with direct memory and latency tradeoffs for deployment. The present evidence is a single preprint, limited to two calibrated policies in held-out simulation and a separate two-checkpoint robot study; the rule is conditional and defers uncertain cases.
limitations: The empirical results are author-reported; no independent execution or reproduction was performed in this review.
The held-out prediction set covers only two calibrated policies and 28 configurations; all seven deferred cases needed closed-loop evidence to settle their outcomes.
The decision rule relies on a within-setting label-ordering hypothesis; policy, task, control protocol, observation log or labeling changes may require recalibration.
The real-robot test uses two fine-tuned Cosmos policies and small task-specific trial counts; its deviation groups do not establish population-wide safety or performance preservation.
The absence of statistical significance in low-deviation comparisons does not establish equivalence or non-inferiority.
The public repository was inspected but not run; independent validation of artifacts and reported measurements remains open.
brief.summary: Xu et al. introduce PreDE, which calibrates policy-specific thresholds from a small set of quantized configurations with known closed-loop outcomes, then uses action deviation on a fixed observation log to accept, reject or defer new candidates. In the paper, 21 of 28 held-out configurations across Cosmos Policy and UVA received decisions, all matching their observed labels; seven were deferred, including both acceptable and degraded outcomes. A separate 450-trial Franka Research 3 study reports significant degradation for configurations assigned to high-deviation groups before trials, while low-deviation results were not statistically significant. W4A4 reduced median action-query latency 1.37× and peak memory about 44% on the tested setup. These are author-reported results, conditional on each policy and evaluation setting.

technical.claimed_result: The authors argue that policy-specific behavioral calibration can screen some quantization configurations offline and defer uncertain cases for closed-loop evaluation. They report that nominal bit width alone and a shared deviation threshold fail to explain task outcomes across the tested policies/settings.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper reports 450 robot task trials plus a separate 45-episode resource-measurement collection. On an RTX 5080, W4A4 action-query median latency was 1485 ms versus 2030 ms for bf16; peak allocated memory was 2.93 GB versus 5.19 GB. Full development/calibration costs and total robot-time economics are not reported.
technical.demonstrated_result: The authors report that across 28 held-out Cosmos Policy and UVA configurations, the rule issued 21 decisions (75% coverage), all matching observed acceptable/degraded labels; seven were deferred, comprising three acceptable, one degraded and three unresolved outcomes. In a separate Franka Research 3 study, deviation groups were fixed before 450 trials across two independently fine-tuned Cosmos policies; all tested high-deviation configurations had significant degradation, while low-deviation comparisons did not reach significance and do not establish equivalence. On the RTX 5080 setup, W4A4 reduced median action-query latency from 2030 to 1485 ms (1.37×) and peak allocated memory from 5.19 to 2.93 GB (about 44%). These are paper-reported results.
technical.implementation_status: Authors provide a public Apache-2.0 GitHub repository with Python package, adapters, examples and tests. The repository landing page and README were inspected; the research desk did not execute the code or reproduce the results.
technical.mechanism: PreDE replays a fixed log of observations through a reference and quantized policy and measures action deviation. It calibrates two thresholds using quantized configurations with known closed-loop labels for a fixed policy, task distribution, control protocol and outcome rule. New configurations below the acceptance threshold are accepted, above the rejection threshold are rejected, and those between are deferred to closed-loop testing. The interpretation depends on a within-setting single-crossing label-ordering hypothesis.
technical.novelty: Calibrates offline action deviation to policy-specific closed-loop outcomes, and explicitly abstains when development evidence cannot distinguish acceptable from degraded behavior; separates quantization deviation measurement from task-performance prediction.
technical.regime: Five world action models across four benchmark settings; held-out prediction covers 20 Cosmos Policy and eight UVA configurations on LIBERO-10, with thresholds calibrated from policy-specific development outcomes. A separate physical study tests two independently fine-tuned Cosmos policies on a Franka Research 3 for cup placement and cube selection. The real-robot deviation groups are prospective but are not the same as PreDE’s calibrated threshold rule.
technical.reproducibility: The paper gives methods, thresholds, benchmark results and a public repository, but no independent reproduction was performed. Threshold validity depends on an explicit within-setting label-ordering hypothesis and recalibration when policy, task or measurement protocol changes.
technical.strongest_baseline: For prediction, the paper compares PreDE with post hoc fixed deviation and bit-width rules at 100% coverage; those rules falsely rejected six and five acceptable held-out candidates, respectively. Quantization outcomes are compared with matched bf16 references and task-specific closed-loop success.

brief.title: PreDE reports a policy-specific gate for screening robot-policy quantization before closed-loop tests
brief.why_it_matters: Robot-policy quantization can save memory and latency, but nominal bit width does not predict task loss consistently. A calibrated offline screen could help prioritize expensive closed-loop evaluations, provided its abstentions, policy-specific scope and finite-trial uncertainty remain visible.
